# California gaming — the CGCC regulator layer

*Built 2026-08-07. Code: `code/103_build_california_gaming.py`.*

*Raw: `data/raw/external/ca_gaming/` (181 documents, `_SOURCE_MANIFEST.csv`
with md5 on every row). Outputs: `data/clean/ca_gaming_payments.csv`,
`data/clean/ca_gaming_facilities_official.csv`,
`review/ca_gaming_unresolved_2026-08-07.csv`,
`data/interim/103_run_summary.txt`, `data/interim/103_zone_log.csv`,
`data/interim/103_sdf_local_mitigation_unverified.csv`.*

*Codebook: `docs/codebooks/07d_california_gaming.md` (regenerated by
`code/41_build_codebooks.py`). Companion to
`docs/COMPACT_TERMS_BUILD_LOG.md` §5, which named this gap, and to
`docs/GAMING_CAPACITY_OFFICIAL_LOG.md`, whose state table said California
published "zero numeric counts."*

Numbers here are reproduced from `data/interim/103_run_summary.txt`, which the
script writes on every run. Re-run rather than edit a figure.

---

## 1. Why this exists, and what closed

`code/95_parse_compact_terms.py` mapped 4,121 reporting obligations across 27
states and found the largest unworked seam in the gaming dataset:

> **California carries 171 compacts with a reporting obligation and Cedar held
> no California regulator file at all.**

It is also the largest tribal gaming market in the country — NIGC's Sacramento
region reported $12.631B across 88 operations in FY2025, the biggest of the
eight regions. Every other large gaming state already had at least one
regulator file.

That gap is now closed. **181 CGCC documents are on disk and 40,164
tribe-identified payment rows publish, spanning 2001-03-22 to 2026-06-30 across
92 distinct quarters.**

| | n |
|---|---:|
| Documents retrieved (all 200, 0 failures, md5 on every row) | 181 |
| RSTF quarterly distribution staff reports | 114 |
| RSTF shortfall notifications | 22 |
| Tribal Nation Grant Fund disbursement reports | 16 |
| SDF reports and fund-balance notifications | 8 |
| CGCC rosters (casinos ×2, RSTF-eligible, tribes making payments) | 4 |
| **Payment rows published** | **40,164** |
| — RSTF, tribes paying **in** | 11,788 |
| — RSTF, tribes paid **out** | 28,124 |
| — TNGF grant disbursements | 252 |
| **Facility roster rows** | **245** |
| Rows keyed to a spine entity | 35,730 (89%) |
| Distinct tribes on the payer side | 62 |
| Distinct tribes on the recipient side | 89 |
| Distinct TNGF grantees | 70 |
| Rows missing `source_url` or `source_quote` | **0** |

## 2. The finding that matters most: California publishes a transfer between
Native governments, in both directions

The Revenue Sharing Trust Fund is funded by gaming tribes and paid to
non-gaming and limited-gaming tribes. **Both sides are Native governments.**
That is a category of flow no federal dataset can see, and it is the reason
`direction` is a column here rather than an assumption:

- **`paid_in`** — CGCC's own exhibit *"Amount of Revenue from Each Compact
  Tribe Received by the Commission"*, 62 tribes, fiscal-year-to-date and
  inception-to-date, 2001 onward. **This is the contributor list, and it is the
  half nobody else publishes.**
- **`paid_out`** — *"Total Amount of Distribution ... Eligible Recipient Indian
  Tribe"*, 89 tribes, per quarter, split into the part funded by license-fee
  revenue and the part funded by a Special Distribution Fund shortfall transfer.

**49 of the 73 tribes on CGCC's RSTF-eligible roster have `N/A` in the casino
column.** They operate no casino and receive money anyway. Scoping California
entity resolution to casino operators would have discarded most of the
recipient side, and that is not a match failure — it is the fund working as
designed.

The Tribal Nation Grant Fund is a third series: 252 discretionary grants to 70
tribes, FY2018/19 → FY2025/26, each with an application title and, from
FY2024/25, a disbursement date. Five programmes (equal distribution, emergency
response, COVID-19 emergency, capacity building, impact) are separate metrics,
never pooled.

**RSTF, TNGF and SDF are three different funds and are never summed.** RSTF and
TNGF pay tribes; SDF pays local government (§6).

## 3. No California payment yields a revenue figure, and finding that out took
reading the compact clauses one at a time

Spec 9.4 allows `payment / rate` as exact arithmetic where the compact makes an
invertible flat rate against a stated base. **The answer for California is that
none of it survives, and the route to that answer is the point.**

`compact_structured_terms.csv` marks **51 California rate rows
`INVERTIBLE_FLAT_RATE`** — correctly, by its own test: one rate in the
instrument, no bracket table, no per-device component in the clause. Joining
those rates to CGCC's RSTF receipts produced 795 tribe-level revenue figures
that looked entirely publishable, each carrying a live URL and a verbatim
clause.

Reading the retained quotes one by one showed **every one of them is a marginal
base**:

> *"six percent (6.0 %) of its Net Win from the operation of Gaming Devices
> **in excess of three hundred fifty (350)**"*

> *"an annual payment of thirty-six million, seven hundred thousand dollars
> ($36,700,000.00); **and** an annual payment for the operation of the
> **additional** Gaming Devices identified in subdivision … fifteen percent
> (15 %) of the Net Win"*

The rate applies to the win from devices **above a threshold**, and in the 15 %
instruments it sits beside a fixed annual sum. So `payment / rate` recovers the
win on the marginal devices only — not the tribe's Net Win — and **no published
device count exists that would let anyone gross it up**, because California's
Gaming Device licences come from a statewide draw pool and even the authorised
count is an entitlement rather than a floor.

The scale of the error avoided is easy to state. San Manuel's FY2025-26 RSTF
receipt of $19,000,000 divided by 15 % gives $126.7M, which would have been
published as that nation's annual Net Win. It is not; it is the win on devices
above the compact's threshold. **The figure would have understated the largest
operators by an order of magnitude while carrying a correct citation** — the
most dangerous shape of error this project has, because the output looks like a
fact.

Two further guards fire behind that one:

- **Deposit disjunction.** The 2016-onward compacts read *"pay … for deposit
  into the Revenue Sharing Trust Fund **or** the Tribal Nation Grant Fund"*.
  CGCC's exhibit reports RSTF receipts only, so an RSTF receipt is a lower
  bound on the obligation, never the obligation. `bound_basis =
  rstf_receipts_only_compact_permits_deposit_into_rstf_or_tngf`.
- **Fund match.** Tule River's only surviving flat rate is 0.5 % of net win
  into a local *Impact Mitigation Fund*. Dividing an RSTF receipt by it would
  cross two different obligations. `bound_basis =
  rate_governs_a_different_fund_than_the_payment`.

Result, and it is the honest one:

```
derived tribe-level revenue rows      0
derived PROPERTY revenue rows         0
TRIBE_LEVEL_REVENUE               9,222
BOUNDED_DERIVED_REVENUE             938   (929 marginal base, 6 per-device
                                           component, 3 wrong fund)
```

**A payment publishes as a payment.** That is what California discloses.

## 4. Five extraction defects, each of which would have shipped wrong numbers

Every one was caught by the same discipline the Michigan and Arizona builds
established: read word positions, assign every number to a column by its
**right** edge, and **foot the result against the document's own printed Totals
row**. 209 of 244 money zones foot exactly; 28 do not and are refused rather
than published; the rest carry no printed total. Every zone's status is in
`data/interim/103_zone_log.csv`.

**(a) The exhibit number is not stable across editions.** Through the 2000s the
payer table is *Exhibit 3* and the fund condition statement is *Exhibit 2*; by
the 2020s the payer table is *Exhibit 2* and the fund condition statement is
*Exhibit 3*. Keying on the number would have swapped a money table for a
balance sheet halfway through a 25-year series. Zones are classified by their
own caption text instead.

**(b) The memo on page 1 is not an exhibit.** A first pass classified any line
that read like an exhibit heading. Page 1 of every staff report is a memo whose
SUBJECT line reads *"...Distribution of Funds to Non-Compact Tribes (Eligible
Recipient Indian Tribes) for the Quarter Ended June 30, 2006"* and whose next
paragraph states *"$10,839,371.91"*. That opened a zone on the memo and swept
narrative sentences in as data rows: **4,029 rows landed under an unrecognised
column layout and not one zone footed.** A zone now begins only at a line that
*starts* with `Exhibit N`.

**(c) A tribe name that wraps puts its money on the second line.** `Bear River
Band of the / Rohnerville Rancheria 117,531.46 …` read one line at a time
labels the payment *"Rohnerville Rancheria"* and drops *"Bear River Band"* —
and the resolver would then key the money to whatever the fragment resolves to.
The unfinished name is carried onto the line carrying numbers. It is reset at
every page break, because a wrapped name never crosses one but the column
header is reprinted on every page: carrying across the break produced labels
like *"Recipient Indian Tribe Received Shortfall Distribution September 30,
2008 Cortina Rancheria"*.

**(d) An exact-zero cell contains only `.00`.** These reports are Excel exports
and the content stream of a zero cell genuinely lacks the leading glyph.
Verified character by character in the 29th staff report: span `.00` at
x = [275.8, 289.7], right edge identical to every other cell in that column.
Only `.0` and `.00` are accepted as zero; any other bare decimal fragment is
refused, because there the missing leading digits would change the value.

**(e) The row whose name and numbers sit on different baselines reads as a
Totals row.** With an empty label, `Cahuilla Band of Indians 0.00 125,000.00`
became the printed total of Exhibit 2 and was compared against a $47.9M column;
20 zones failed on it. The carry is now resolved before the total test. A
related fix: CGCC prints the currency symbol in its own cell, so the label is
`Totals $` rather than `Totals`, and requiring a bare `Totals` sent zones to
compare against **`Grand Totals`**, which adds interest income and is not the
column sum.

## 5. What California suppresses, and how that is recorded

From the 2016 reports on, CGCC prints `--` with footnote 2 against several
compact tribes and reports their combined figure on one *"Aggregate Total for
Tribes"* line.

**Suppressed is not zero, and the two must never be conflated.** 318 rows carry
`value_suppressed_by_regulator = yes` with a blank value: the obligation and
the period are published, the amount is not. The aggregate line is kept —
without it the report's own Totals row does not foot — as 40 rows typed
`recipient_type = aggregate_of_suppressed_tribes` and flagged
`not_a_single_tribe`. It is never attributed to any tribe.

This is a real disclosure fact about California and it belongs in the dataset,
not in a footnote nobody reads.

---

## 6. The Special Distribution Fund does not name the tribe. This overturns the
brief's expectation.

The brief expected county-level SDF allocations to name the tribe whose
facility generated them. **They do not.**

CGCC's 2015 report to the Joint Legislative Budget Committee carries thirteen
appendices of SDF local mitigation grants, FY2003/04 → FY2014/15. Every row is
**county → local agency → project → amount**:

```
Riverside   Co of Riverside - Sheriff Dept   Deputies, Patrol Car, Equip   1,996,061.00
            City of Temecula                 Wolf Creek Fire Station         380,641.00
            City of Coachella                Motorcycle Officer              245,191.00
```

No tribe appears anywhere in the appendix. Attaching a Riverside County
fire-district grant to a tribe would be an inference from geography and nothing
else, and Riverside County hosts many gaming tribes.

**1,292 line items were parsed and none published.** They are written to
`data/interim/103_sdf_local_mitigation_unverified.csv` so the next pass starts
from the parse rather than from the retrieval. A second, independent reason to
withhold: the line items do not foot against the printed per-county totals in
this pass, because a three-column layout (Amount Paid / Amt Allocated / Amt
Reverted) beside a free-text purpose column defeats the leftmost-money rule.

The consequence for the model is worth stating plainly: **SDF is not a
facility-attributable series in anything California publishes.** RSTF is
tribe-level; SDF is county-level; they are separate `fund` values and are never
summed.

---

## 7. CGCC does publish at facility level — identity, never capacity

`data/clean/ca_gaming_facilities_official.csv`, 245 rows from four dated
rosters:

| roster | rows | as of |
|---|---:|---|
| Tribal Casino Locations (alphabetical by tribe, and by casino) | 131 | 2025-01-23 |
| RSTF Eligible Tribes | 73 | 2025-11-13 |
| Tribes Currently Making Compact or Secretarial Procedures Payments | 41 | 2024-11-05 |

They carry **tribe ↔ casino ↔ city ↔ county**, dated, and — in the payments
list — **which fund each tribe pays into**: 34 tribes ticked for SDF, 31 for
RSTF. Which fund is read from *which column* the tick sits in, never from how
many ticks a row carries; most payers pay into only one of the two, and
counting glyphs would have made every single-tick tribe an SDF payer.

**They carry no numeric capacity of any kind** — no device counts, no revenue,
no square footage. `measurement_type` is deliberately blank on every row: a
roster is identity, not a measurement. The state table in
`GAMING_CAPACITY_OFFICIAL_LOG.md` remains correct on that point.

**180 of 245 rows attach to an existing `CCP-`/`VP-` property** (132 by exact
name within California, 48 as the tribe's sole California property). No new
property universe was created and `gaming_facilities.csv` was not touched. 57
unresolved casino names go to the review queue with the tribe's California
properties listed as candidates; 5 rows are tribes with no casino, which is
correct rather than a failure.

Three roster defects worth carrying forward, all from the same cause — the
column layout is not the same in the three files:

- **Column names come from the printed header, not from ordinal position.**
  Reading the third column as "city" because it was third filed all 65 casino
  names under `casino_county` in one file and left `casino_city` empty in
  another.
- **A two-line header can arrive in either order.** `CASINO` over `COUNTY`
  reassembles as `CASINO COUNTY` or `COUNTY CASINO` depending on span order;
  anchored whole-string patterns matched neither, the county column went
  unnamed, and county text merged into city. Token tests, most specific first.
- **A record with several casinos is cut on the city column's baselines**, and
  a split that produces a facility named after its own city is refused
  outright. Agua Caliente lists three casinos whose name lines lead the city
  lines by more than one baseline; the split slipped by one and produced a
  casino called *"Rancho Mirage"*. That record is emitted once, unsplit, as
  `multi_casino_unsplit_needs_ruling`.

## 8. Entity resolution, and one guard that had to be narrowed after measurement

`resolve_entity` is imported from `code/33_apply_party_rulings.py`. **No second
matcher was written.** What was added is data and refusals:

- The spine's `fr_official_name` is folded into `aliases` before resolution.
  That is not a matcher — the resolver already consults aliases, and CGCC
  writes the Federal Register long form while the spine's `canonical_name` is
  often one or two words.
- **Refusals**, not guesses: an entity class a gaming payment cannot be about
  (7 refusals, Urban Indian Organization and a BIE school — the Chickasaw
  Children's Village defect), a cross-state resolution (1, to New Mexico), a
  containment match where the record is not at least as specific as the entity
  (2).

**The short-name collision guard had to be narrowed, and the narrowing was
measured.** Refusing every containment match onto one of the spine's 281 staged
short-name collisions refused **472 California names outright** — Bear River,
Cahto, Augustine, La Posta, Ramona, Scotts Valley — because that list is
exactly the set of tribes whose canonical name is one or two words, which in
California is most of them. A collision is only dangerous when the record does
not say *which* colliding entity it means. The refusal now applies only where
the record fails to carry the entity's own Federal Register long-form tokens:
*"Bear River Band of the Rohnerville Rancheria"* carries them and resolves; a
bare *"Bear River"* does not and is refused. Refusals fell 472 → 87 and rows
keyed rose from 25,269 to 35,730.

`NAME_TRAPS` is imported from `cedar_domain` and its members — *rancheria*,
*santa*, *san*, *little*, *central* — are stripped before any specificity test,
so they can never carry a match on their own.

Every row is `confidence_tier = B`. These are algorithmic extractions with
receipts, not human rulings. **Nothing here publishes without a review pass.**

`review/ca_gaming_unresolved_2026-08-07.csv` — 206 rows, blank `YOUR_RULING`:

| n | reason |
|---:|---|
| 87 | short-name collision the record does not disambiguate |
| 74 | no spine match — mostly historical CGCC names (`Rumsey Rancheria`, `Smith River Rancheria`, `Cortina Rancheria`, `Barona Band of Mission Indians`) that are alias rulings, not new entities |
| 20 | ambiguous containment (`Capitan Grande` / `Capitan Grande Band`, `California Valley` / `Coyote Valley`) |
| 14 | casino name not matched to a Cedar property, candidates listed |
| 7 | refused entity class |
| 4 | cross-state, over-broad containment, ambiguous core |

## 9. Rules honoured

- **Zero fabrication.** 0 of 40,164 payment rows and 0 of 245 facility rows are
  missing `source_url` or `source_quote`. Asserted in the build, not checked
  afterwards.
- **A cap is never a count.** `may_promote(AUTHORIZED_MAXIMUM,
  ACTIVE_FLOOR_COUNT)` and the same for `PROJECTED` are asserted at import.
  California's device licences come from a statewide draw pool, so an
  authorised count is an entitlement — and CGCC publishes no device counts at
  all, so the question does not arise in this file.
- **No property revenue on a tribe-level base.** Asserted per row: zero rows
  carry `EXACT_DERIVED_PROPERTY_REVENUE`.
- **A factual bound is not a confidence interval.** Every
  `BOUNDED_DERIVED_REVENUE` row names what blocks the inversion in
  `bound_basis`. No interval is computed anywhere and no model exists.
- **Cumulative figures are extracted, footed, and withheld by flag.** 11,809
  inception-to-date rows carry `cumulative_do_not_sum`. A cumulative published
  beside a quarterly figure is a double count waiting to happen, and a
  cumulative payment divided by a rate is a cumulative revenue.
- **Exclusions are columns, never deletions.** 1,927 rows superseded by a
  REVISED staff report stay readable and flagged.
- **Attach, never create.** No new property IDs. `gaming_facilities.csv`,
  `gaming_capacity_official.csv`, `compact_structured_terms.csv`,
  `compact_required_reports.csv`, `nigc_*`, `entity_aliases.csv`,
  `entity_relationships.csv`, the identifier ledger and the spine were **read
  only**. `code/01_build_entity_spine.py` was not run. The 316 compact PDFs
  behind CGCC's compacts page were deliberately not downloaded — the compact
  corpus belongs to another build — though the page itself is saved, because it
  is a dated tribe → governing-instrument roster and that is what makes the
  invertibility join possible at all.
- **Pull discipline.** One poller, single stream, 1.6 s minimum gap,
  `logs/_HOSTLOCK_cgcc.ca.gov.json` and `_HOSTLOCK_oag.ca.gov.json` claimed
  before the first request. `api.usaspending.gov` was not touched. No process
  was killed by image name.
- **`code/62_no_regression_check.py`** was run before and after and is
  unchanged: the single standing failure, `codebook_undocumented_public = 10`,
  is pre-existing and belongs to datasets 06 and 12. This build added 58
  variables and documented every published one; `codebook_variables` rose
  1,032 → 1,099.

## 10. Known limits and what is next, in value order

1. **28 money zones do not foot and are refused.** They are named with their
   per-column arithmetic in `data/interim/103_zone_log.csv`. Several are off by
   a single tribe's $275,000 quarterly distribution or by exactly $1.00 in
   CGCC's own printed total; each needs one hand read. Recovering them extends
   the recipient series past the gaps.
2. **890 unmapped-column events** come from four Exhibit-1 zones whose banding
   found 5 or 11 columns rather than 4 — a stray number widening the model. The
   zones are refused, so nothing wrong publishes.
3. **74 no-spine-match names are alias rulings, not new entities.** `Rumsey
   Rancheria` is Yocha Dehe; `Smith River Rancheria` is Tolowa Dee-ni'. CGCC
   itself prints the renames as *"(previously listed as …)"* in its recent
   files, which is a ready-made alias source for whoever owns
   `entity_aliases.csv`.
4. **The SDF appendices need a three-column reader** that foots against the
   printed per-county totals. Even then no tribe is recoverable — the value is
   a county-level impact-mitigation series, not an allocation.
5. **The California DOJ Bureau of Gambling Control was reached
   (`oag.ca.gov/gambling`, `oag.ca.gov/gambling/tribal`, both HTTP 200) and
   publishes no document links at all** on those pages —
   `oag.ca.gov/gambling/publications` is a 404. Tribal casino licensing and any
   device or facility counts are not published there in retrievable form. This
   is a documented negative, not an unchecked box.
6. **The State Controller and Department of Finance route is unworked.** DOF's
   *Notification of Available Fund Balance for the Indian Gaming Special
   Distribution Fund* letters are held (2015–2020) and are scanned budget
   tables in aggregate — several have no usable text layer and would need OCR,
   and none name a tribe.

---

## 11. What California structurally does not publish

Stated plainly so nobody re-checks it:

- **No gaming device counts, of any kind, anywhere.** Not per tribe, not per
  casino, not statewide. The 1999 licence pool draw results are not published.
- **No gaming revenue.** Not per property, not per tribe, not statewide. The
  only revenue-shaped number on CGCC's tribal page is `GGR24_080425.pdf`, which
  is a **re-hosted NIGC national report** with eight regional aggregates and
  nothing Californian in it. (Already recorded as a dead end in
  `GAMING_CAPACITY_OFFICIAL_LOG.md`; confirmed again here.)
- **No per-tribe payment to the State.** The compacts' General Fund and Special
  Distribution Fund obligations are not published tribe by tribe. What is
  published tribe by tribe is the RSTF, and — as a yes/no tick, not an amount —
  which tribes pay into SDF at all.
- **No tribe behind an SDF local mitigation grant.** §6.
- **Individual amounts for the tribes CGCC suppresses.** §5.

What California *does* publish, uniquely among the states worked so far, is
**tribe-identified money for tribes that operate no casino**, quarterly, for a
quarter of a century.
